correctness.rationale: Four transition classes exactly partition feasible edges conditional on (X,Y), giving the three finite-size drift identities. All normalized jumps are at most 2/n and aggregate rates at most (1+c)n, ensuring \(O(1/n)\) martingale variance on compact times. Global Lipschitz drift then proves ODE convergence. The infinite-time tail is bounded by still-unmatched vertices X_n(T)/n, while deterministic \(x(T)\le1/(1+T)\). Integration of \((x+z)'=-x^2\) proves the exact loss, and \(x'\ge-(1+c)x\) proves \(1-f(c)\ge 1/[2(1+c)]\). Independent rational recurrences agree in 24 finite tests; their role is verification rather than proof.

value.rationale: The same exponential planted-matching disorder supports almost-perfect recovery by global minimum-sum matching at every \(c\ge4\), but irreversible sequential adsorption loses at least \(1/[2(1+c)]\) of the target edges asymptotically at each fixed finite c. The exact kinetic fluid curve and a strictly positive quantitative deficit identify a physical/algorithmic obstruction not visible in final matching cardinality (which is always n). This is a structural infinite-family theorem, not a renamed textbook identity or isolated enumeration.
